attributes.name: Druva - Repeated Failed Administrator Logins
attributes.description: Detects repeated failed Druva administrator login attempts originating from the same source IP address. Multiple authentication failures within a short period may indicate brute-force attacks, password spraying, credential stuffing, or an attempt to compromise an administrator account.
author: Druva
false_positives: An administrator repeatedly entering an incorrect password.
A recently changed password leaving stale credentials in a client or automation.
Authentication or integration testing performed by authorized personnel.
attributes.query:
FROM logs-druva.event-*
| WHERE druva.feature == "Admin Event"
    AND druva.event_type == "Admin Login"
    AND event.outcome == "failure"
    AND event.id IS NOT NULL
    AND source.ip IS NOT NULL

| EVAL principal = COALESCE(
    TO_STRING(user.email),
    TO_STRING(user.name)
  )

| WHERE principal IS NOT NULL

| STATS
    failed_attempts = COUNT_DISTINCT(event.id),
    first_failure = MIN(@timestamp),
    last_failure = MAX(@timestamp)
  BY principal, source.ip

| WHERE failed_attempts >= 5
attributes.note:
### Investigation guide

This rule detects at least five distinct failed Druva administrator authentication attempts associated with the same principal and source IP. Repeated failures may indicate password guessing or other attempts to obtain administrator access.

#### Investigation steps

- Identify the administrator principal, source IP, failure count, and time range.
- Determine whether the source IP is expected for the administrator.
- Review successful logins by the same account or source after the failures.
- Check whether the administrator recently changed credentials or reported authentication problems.
- Review other administrator accounts receiving failures from the same source.
- Search for sensitive administrative activity if a successful login follows.

#### Response

- Contact the administrator through a trusted channel when compromise is suspected.
- Reset or rotate credentials according to organizational policy.
- Investigate the source IP and any successful sessions associated with the activity.
